correctness.rationale: The overlap graph has exactly the stated edge set, is balanced and strongly connected. Rooting each cyclic Euler tour by the unique all-zero labeled edge removes all rotation multiplicities. The fixed-first-edge last-exit/BEST bijection has unit local factorials. Each weight-two vertex has its unique zero outgoing edge, forcing a finite route to weight-one or zero. Contracted branches are exactly \(j\mapsto j-1\) (zero) and \(j\mapsto m-1-j\) (one). A low-index one-choice traps an invariant interval disjoint from the root; with all low choices zero, every chosen branch strictly decreases, so every high choice is independent. This proves the exact formula for all \(k\ge2\). Full original-graph integer cofactors through k=11, independent low-branch exhaustive checks through k=15, and circular factor brute enumerations through k=7 reproduce it, but finite testing is not used as infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The original 2013 paper treats the exact family but proves existence and constructs some cycles, not total enumeration. The 2018 manuscript derives eight successor rules for bounded-weight classes without evaluating all in-trees. A 2025 paper explicitly uses general in-tree sampling and describes the arbitrary-Eulerian mechanism, but not the special reflection-interval classification or 2-power evaluation. Searches of relevant records and web for aliases, exact formula and the higher/lower generality did not locate a dominating or equal theorem. Residual risk of unindexed equivalent tree-count is acknowledged.

value.rationale: The weight-at-most-two family is an established natural weight-range universal-cycle object, and the exact number of globally distinct cyclic solutions was not determined by the cited constructions. The all-order 2-power count and explicit free-choice classification give both finite-block structure and efficient uniform sampling without general spanning-tree sampling. These are motivated graph-specific invariants, not an arbitrary numerical slice, a known-table recomputation, or merely an implementation of the BEST theorem.
